requirements.requirement: On node1, an HTTPS web service listens on TCP port 8443 and returns exactly `secure-os-comparison-ready` at `/`.
requirements.summary: Direct requests to node1's managed IP returned HTTP 200 with the exact required body, and a wildcard TCP 8443 listener was observed both before and after an actual reboot.

requirements.requirement: The HTTPS endpoint uses a certificate trusted by node1's system trust store.
requirements.summary: The certificate has DNS and IP SANs for node1, verifies against the system CA bundle, and ordinary curl requests without disabled validation succeeded before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The independent restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot was acknowledged, disruption was observed, the boot ID changed, and the service, listener, firewall, trust verification, certificate identity, and exact response recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: HTTPS was tested from node1 against its own managed IP rather than from a separate client. The wildcard listener and runtime/permanent firewall checks support off-node availability, but do not directly exercise it.

Native package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be independently compared; the command audit shows no package installation or removal.

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found no unnecessary mutations. The service account/directories, PKI and trust anchor, application, systemd unit, and firewall rule directly implement the requested endpoint; the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The three failed commands were read-only availability polls during reboot. No abandoned troubleshooting change was found, so there is no unnecessary mutation to report as retained or reverted. The final snapshot shows no failed units, only the intended new listener, and normal systemd PrivateTmp entries.
